title: Harmonic conductor for staggered token waves and NCCL eclipsing
creator: Ava Chen
description: Introduce a coordinated scheduling layer ("Harmonic Conductor") that smooths NCCL traffic and phases tensor/pipeline parallel stages to reduce tail latency for mixed prefill+decode workloads. The conductor will proactively stagger prefill microbatches, align attention-kernel selection across ranks, and inject lightweight rendezvous padding when beneficial to prevent NCCL contention spikes ("eclipsing"). This ticket covers design, prototype, microbenchmarks, and an initial canary rollout plan on Dedicated clusters.
acceptance_criteria:
1) End-to-end prototype reduces 99th percentile token latency by >= 12% on mixed prefill+decode traces in internal benchmark harness.
2) No regression (>3%) in throughput for steady-state decode-only workloads.
3) Observability: per-rank NCCL bytes/time, rendezvous padding events, and kernel-selection logs visible in Console dashboards.
4) Canary rollout plan documented and automated fallback to default scheduler implemented.
5) PR with tests and microbenchmark results merged into runtime-1.20 branch.
notes: Key ideas: 1) compute a lightweight per-request phase vector derived from token window size + pipeline stage map; 2) prefer attention kernels that reduce cross-rank bandwidth when scheduling overlapping NCCL windows; 3) use transient rendezvous padding (no-op microbatches) to avoid large concurrent NCCL allreduces when traffic predicts contention; 4) maintain deterministic fallbacks to existing conductor for safety. We must validate quantization-sensitive kernels don't get penalized by phase alignment heuristics.
